units.title: Basic Concepts of Data Structures
topics: 1.6. Analysis Terms (for the definitions purpose only): a. Time Complexity b. Space Complexity c. Asymptotic Notations: Big Oh Notation, Big Omega Notation, Big Theta Notation, Best case Time Complexity, Average case Time Complexity, Worst case Time Complexity
1.7. Array: i. Row Major Arrays ii. Column Major Arrays
1.9. Searching an element into an array: i. Linear Search ii. Binary Search
uos: 1.a. Represent the data in relevant memory
1.b. Differentiate primitive and non-primitive data structures
1.c. List key features of an algorithm
1.d. Define time complexity and space complexity
1.e. Implement programs to represent array in row major and column major order
1.f. Design and Implement search algorithms

units.title: Strings
topics: 2.1. String representation: Reading and Writing Strings

2.2. String operations : Finding length of a string, Converting Characters of a string into upper case and lower case, Concatenation of two strings to form a new string, Appending, Reversing a string, Copying a string, Comparing strings, Insertion, Substring, Deletion Data Structures and Algorithms Course Code: 4330704
uos: 2.a. Describe representation of a strings
2.b. Develop algorithms to implement various operations on string

units.title: Stack and Queues
topics: 3.2. Stack : Array representation of Stack, PUSH- POP Operations on Stack, Implementation of Stack, Application of Stack, Infix, Prefix and Postfix Forms of Expressions, Recursive Functions (Factorial, greatest common divisor, Fibonacci series) 3c.. Implement different operations on a Queue
3.3. Queue: Array representation of Queue Operations on a Queue (Add an element, delete an element, display all elements of a queue), Implementation of a Queue, Limitation of a Single Queue
3.6. Differentiate circular queue and simple queue
uos: 3.a. Define linear and non- linear data structures
3.b. Implement algorithms to push an element into stack, pop an element from the stack.
3.c. Differentiate circular and simple queue

units.title: Linked List
topics: 4.7. Basic operations on singly linked list : Insertion of a new node in the beginning of the list, at the end of the list, after a given node, before a given node, in sorted linked list, Deleting the first and last node from a linked list, Searching a node in Linked List, Count the number of nodes in linked list
4.9. Difference between circular linked list and singly linked list
4.11. Difference between Doubly linked list and singly linked list
uos: 4.a. Define linked list 4.1 Pointers Revision
4.b. Implement algorithms to perform various operations on a singly linked list
4.c. Distinguish circular linked list and singly linked list
4.d. Distinguish Doubly linked list and singly linked list
4.e. List applications of the linked list

units.title: Trees
topics: 5.2. Basic Terms: General Tree, Forest, Binary trees, level number, degree, in-degree and out-degree, root node, leaf node, directed edge, path, depth Binary tree: Complete Binary Tree, Strict Binary Tree, Conversion of General Tree to Binary Tree Data Structures and Algorithms Course Code: 4330704
5.3. Binary Search Tree : Insertion of a node in binary tree, Deletion of a node in binary tree, Searching a node in binary tree
5.4. Binary Tree Traversal : Inorder, Preorder, Postorder
uos: 5.a. Define non-linear data structure
5.b. Define basic terms of a tree data structure
5.c. Convert general tree to binary tree
5.d. Implement basic operations on a binary tree
5.e. Demonstrate the traversal of a binary tree
5.f. List applications of tree

units.title: Sorting and Hashing
topics: 6.1. Sorting Methods : a. Bubble Sort, b. Selection Sort, c. Quick Sort, d. Insertion Sort, e. Merge Sort, f. Radix Sort

6.3. Hash functions: Division Method, Middle Square Method, Folding Method Note: The UOs need to be formulated at the ‘Application Level’ and above of Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy’ to accelerate the attainment of the COs and the competency.
uos: 6.a. Arrange data in ascending and descending orders using appropriate sorting algorithm
6.b. Apply various hashing techniques
